chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.summary: Introduction Seven years ago I wrote a book called The Most Important Thing: Uncommon Sense for the Thoughtful Investor, regarding where investors should direct their greatest attention. In it I said “the most important thing is being attentive to cycles.” The truth, however, is that I applied the label “the most important thing” to nineteen other things as well. Every one of the twenty elements I discussed in The Most Important Thing is absolutely essential for anyone who wishes to be a successful investor. chapters.title: Putting It All Together—The Market Cycle
chapters.summary: Our job as investors is simple: to deal with the prices of assets, assessing where they stand today and making judgments regarding how they will change in the future. Fundamentals, which I’ve been calling “events,” can largely be reduced to earnings, cash flow, and the outlook for the two. They are affected by many things, including trends in the economy, profitability and the availability of capital. The themes behind the cycles’ behavior—and the ways in which they interact and combine—have a repeating, understandable pattern, as we have discussed at length. They all come together—and they combine with idiosyncratic and random influences—to cause the behavior of the securities market. Investing, as I’ve said, consists of positioning capital so as to benefit from future events.
